newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Fleeing Zairean soldiers leave trail of chaos.
newsitem.headline: Fleeing Zairean soldiers leave trail of chaos.

text.p: Zairean soldiers, who have sown terror while retreating from rebel forces, raped elderly nuns and tortured a seminarian before fleeing in the robes of their victims, survivors recounted on Monday.

"We only came out of hiding in the bush yesterday," Abbot Jean-Chrisostome Wambereki told Reuters at the Roman Catholic mission of Our Lady of Peace in Maboya not far from the eastern Zaire's border with Uganda.

"It was after a month of our hiding there. Our mission was attacked first from November 8 to 10, and then again on the 27 November. Both times it was by Zairean paratroopers and by the presidential guard.

"The first time they came, they tortured a lay priest for money," said the Abbot. "Brother Ezekiel was in the rectory, tidying after supper. They came and demanded money, they smashed him in the face with a rifle butt. Then they beat him in the kidneys with sticks and they tried to crush his testicles."
The Zairean troops were fleeing the advance of Mai-Mai tribal withcraft fighters at the head of rebel forces.
The Zairean soldiers also ransacked the convent of the Little Sisters of the Visitation, next to the mission.
"The Zairean paratroops stole everything," said a nun at the small convent who gave her name as Sister Angela.
"They attacked the nuns, stole their clothing -- even two pairs of womens' shoes. Six military went from room to room, and smashed one of the nuns in the face when she would not give any money.

"They stole nuns' robes and some of them put them on over their camouflage uniforms as they fled. All of us tried to run into the bush including some of the older sisters, one of whom has rheumatism, and two who had malaria," she added.
"They attacked the older nuns, they raped some of them," she said. Some of the nuns were more than 60 years old.
Staff at the mission said nuns at two other convents and mission stations in Butembo region were also raped by soldiers.
The mission and convent at Maboya were attacked again on November 27 by more fleeing Zairean soldiers, who looted and smashed parts of the convent, including a small health centre.
"Six of the nuns are still hiding in the bush. They are terrified," said the abbot. "One of them has gone to hospital."
